transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-14 15:30 UTC, Duration: 58m
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marcus (Product), Tom (OceanBridge CTO), Jules (Infra), Maya (Finance), Ravi (Security)

00:00 Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time today. Happy Valentine's Day by the way. We'll go through a targeted Console demo focused on per-route usage and cost playbooks — how you can attribute spend to product routes, set budgets, and what a hosted vs dedicated decision looks like. Priya's gonna lead the demo.

00:22 Priya (SE): Cool, thanks Alex. Hi Tom, Jules, Maya, Ravi. Quick agenda: one, live tour of route dashboards; two, how cost breakdowns appear (tokens / embedding units / model runtime); three, Optimize recommendations — batching, cache, quantization; four, Q&A and next steps. If anything's garbled please interrupt.

00:45 Tom (Customer): Sounds good. We're specifically interested in tying cost back to our "search-summarize" route and the new "chat-assist" product. Finance wants clean chargeback.

00:58 Priya: Great — I'll open the Console. (typing) Ok landing page, route list on the left. I'm going to filter to the "search-summarize" route. Note: this is a demo dataset, names anonymized. Up top we have throughput and p95 latency. The timeline shows traffic spikes around 02/01 and the right panel shows cost breakdown.

02:10 Priya: The cost tile breaks down tokens generated, embedding compute, and model variant delta. You can click into the "tokens" slice to see token distribution by prompt vs completion, and by customer tenant if you have multi-tenant tagging.

02:40 Jules: Quick question — how accurate is the token accounting? We do a fair bit of prompt templating and sometimes tokens are counted inconsistently across libraries.

02:50 Priya: Good question. We use a combination of runtime token accounting plus optional SDK-side instrumentation. For 1st-party Redwood clients it's usually within 1-3% of raw token counts. For custom SDKs, there can be variance; that's why we have an "upload prompt-set" reconciliation flow where you can feed canonical prompts and we re-run token estimates.

03:24 Tom: Ok. Can you show how we map cost to our internal product codes? We have chargeback for Product A vs Product B.

03:35 Priya: Yep. Under settings -> route tags you can attach product codes or Jira keys. Here I'm adding tag "PB-Search" to the route. Now the Cost Explorer can group by tag. You can export CSV for your internal FinOps system.

04:10 Maya (Finance): The export — does it include breakdowns by model version and quantization settings? We sometimes run cheaper quantized variants for low-accuracy needs.

04:20 Priya: Export includes model_name, model_version, quantization_profile, tokens_in, tokens_out, and cost_estimate per row. We also surface the model performance delta (latency and top-k quality proxy) so you can make tradeoffs.

05:01 Priya: Next I want to show the per-request trace. If you click into an individual bucket you get a sample request list with timestamps, full prompt (redacted if PII), and a link to the trace that shows kv-cache hits, batching window, and which GPU served the request.

05:36 Jules: That trace link is useful. We want to ensure we can attribute overhead from network egress for private deployments.

05:45 Alex: Small note — for Private (VPC) deployments we can surface network egress as an additional cost line if you provide egress pricing or we pull it from your cloud billing via a connector. It's optional but many infra teams like the holistic view.

06:10 Priya: Now, cost playbooks. Console has a Recommendations tab (we call it Optimize). It analyzes route patterns and gives knobs: change batching policy, enable prefix/KV caching, or suggest a quantized model variant. For example, Optimize recommended enabling batching on "search-summarize" with a batch window of 15ms which reduces tokens/sec cost by ~12% in this workload.

07:00 Tom: Is there an automated rollout for these suggestions? We can't just flip quantization globally.

07:10 Priya: We have rollouts — canary % rollout, A/B route split, and automatic rollback on quality regressions tied to a prompt test set. You provide a test prompt set and a metric (e.g., semantic similarity or hallucination rate), and Console will monitor.

07:40 Tom: Who owns the rollback? Is it automatic or do we get alerts?

07:50 Priya: You can choose. Default is alert + manual apply. But for aggressive cost-savings you can opt in to auto-fallback if a defined quality threshold breaches.

08:20 Maya: On the finance side, we care about predictive spend. How good are the forecasts?

08:30 Marcus (Product): Forecasting is based on historical usage patterns with traffic seasonality detection. We provide a baseline forecast and high/low bands. For large customers we can also ingest product event calendars to improve the forecast. The Console also surfaces a model mix scenario builder to compare hosted vs dedicated pricing.

09:05 Priya: Let me demo scenario builder — switch to the 'Economics' tab. Here you can define route traffic projections, select models (e.g., gpt-small-12b-int8 vs gpt-large-16b-fp16), and it will compute per-month cost for hosted API and a dedicated GPU pool (we model reserved v. burst capacity).

09:40 Priya: For a rough rule of thumb: if you have steady throughput above ~8M prompt tokens/month with low latency constraints, Dedicated often makes sense. But it's workload dependent; the builder gives a break-even horizon.

10:10 Tom: Our privacy team is pushing for private deployment — can you summarize security controls?

10:18 Ravi (Security): yes that's my area — what certs and controls are there.

10:22 Alex: For Redwood Private we support VPC peering, SAML SSO (IdP), RBAC with SCIM sync, KMS/HSM integrations for keys, and audit logs shipped to your SIEM. We are SOC 2 Type II compliant and can provide the compliance pack. For on-prem air-gapped installs we have a separate packaging process.

10:50 Ravi: About KMS — does Redwood ever see plaintext model inputs or keys?

11:00 Alex: For Private with customer-managed keys, Redwood's control plane does not have access to your plaintext keys. For hosted customers, data-in-transit is encrypted and we support customer-managed keys for model encryption at rest in some tiers. We'll provide specific diagram in the security pack.

11:30 Jules: For networking, we run strict egress rules and use private link. Any additional steps for peering with Redwood?

11:40 Priya: We'll provide a connectivity checklist — CIDR ranges, firewall rules, proxy-friendly auth flows. That's part of the pilot onboarding doc.

12:05 Priya: Back to the Console — I'm going to open a sample route-level dashboard for "chat-assist". First panel is cost by model variant. You can see previous two weeks we shifted 30% of traffic to a quantized variant and cost dropped accordingly but p95 latency rose slightly.

12:40 Tom: How granular is the cost attribution when one request fans out to multiple model calls? For example we call embedding service then a generation call.

12:52 Priya: Good point. We support multi-hop transactions: a single user request can be linked to child calls in the trace and we aggregate costs across the transaction so a single row in the exported chargeback can reflect combined embedding + generation cost.

13:20 Priya: Now the usage alerts. You can create budget alerts at route level or tag level. For example, set a soft alarm at 60% of monthly budget and hard at 95%. Alerts can page via PagerDuty, send email to finance, or create a Jira ticket.

13:50 Maya: Will alerts include predicted blowout risk (like runway to spend limit)?

14:00 Marcus: Yes the alert payload includes projected burn rate and days-to-budget based on current trajectory.

14:20 Priya: Ok Q&A time — Tom any blockers you foresee for a pilot?

14:30 Tom: Two: network connectivity clearance and legal reviewing the DPA. Also we need confidence in cost modeling accuracy before we commit infra spend.

14:45 Alex: For the DPA we'll send the legal pack. For cost modeling we'll run the 7-day console pilot where you point a small slice of traffic or replay traffic and we generate exact raw token counts and cost attribution. That usually calms Finance.

15:10 Jules: On traffic replay — how do you handle secrets? We don't want real user PII replayed to any external endpoint.

15:20 Priya: We support sanitized replay where prompts are redacted or synthesized, and offline replay inside your VPC if you choose Private. For hosted pilot you can run replay on an anonymized dataset.

15:45 Tom: Can you show the pilot setup UI?

15:50 Priya: Sure. Under onboarding -> pilots. Select '7-day console pilot'. You choose route(s), sample traffic volume, and tagging. There's a checkbox for "anonymize prompts". Once you accept the pilot we'll provision a sandbox console project and a temporary API key.

16:30 Maya: Cost of pilot?

16:35 Alex: Pilot is free for the window — Redwood covers the infra cost for the sandbox, though if you push large volumes we'll discuss a minimal usage surcharge. The pilot includes the Economy scenario report and a workshop to interpret results.

17:00 Priya: I'm going to drill into an example recommendation. Here Optimize suggests enabling prefix cache for the login helpflow — it detects repeated prompts and estimates 22% token savings. If you enable it we can auto-populate a canary that routes 10% of traffic through cached variant.

17:40 Tom: Any caveats on consistency? We care about fresh answers.

17:45 Priya: Cache TTLs are configurable and you can whitelist routes. For conversational contexts we recommend finer granularity (short TTLs) and if freshness is critical we suggest function-call gating or cache bypass.

18:10 Ravi: What about governance — who can toggle these features?

18:20 Alex: RBAC in Console. Roles: Viewer, Operator, Cost Admin, Security Admin. You can require approval workflows for runbook changes. We also maintain audit trails.

18:40 Tom: Ok good. Now let's talk numbers — what's the expected break-even horizon for a 4-node dedicated pool on our traffic profile?

18:52 Priya: From the earlier scenario builder if we assume your sample projection — looks like ~9 months to break even on the committed capacity compared to hosted usage, due to burst credit and reserved discounts. We'll include a sensitivity analysis in the pricing sheet.

19:20 Maya: If we do Dedicated, is there a minimum commitment?

19:25 Alex: We have monthly reserved options and annual tiers. Minimums vary by region and SKU; we'll show you the exact options in the pricing sheet. There's also a burst overlay so you don't have to buy capacity for rare spikes.

20:00 Tom: One last technical: how do you handle model upgrades and pinned versions? We need stable behavior across releases.

20:10 Priya: You can pin model_version at route level. We support canarying a model rollout and you can configure auto-fallback to previous version if evals degrade. Console keeps a version history for reproducibility.

20:40 Alex: Time check — a few quick clarifications then we'll wrap.

20:50 Jules: On the export, can we include internal cost center mapping columns so finance gets a single join key?

20:58 Priya: Yes — we support custom metadata on routes (e.g., cost_center_id) and that'll flow to the CSV export and API.

21:20 Maya: Cool. Also please include a sample invoice mock so we know the line items.

21:30 Alex: We'll attach a sample invoice format in the pricing email.

21:40 Tom: Ok overall this looks promising. What would success look like for the pilot?

21:50 Priya: Typical success criteria: one, accurate route-to-product cost mapping within 5%; two, a validated scenario showing achievable 10-20% unit cost reduction via caching/batching/quantization; three, security sign-off on connectivity and DPA.

22:20 Tom: Those are fair. Let's do it.

22:30 Alex: Great — next steps we already listed in the meeting notes. We'll follow up with the pricing sheet and pilot onboarding link.

22:40 Maya: One ask — can you include an executive one-pager summarizing cost benefits for our CFO?

22:48 Marcus: Absolutely, we'll include a two-pager with charts: break-even, cost per 1M tokens, and recommended configuration.

23:05 Priya: Any final quick technical questions?

23:10 Jules: Nothing else from infra.

23:15 Ravi: Send the compliance pack and answers to the security questionnaire — I'll route internally.

23:22 Alex: Will do. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email and Slack.

23:30 Meeting end.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-hearings of product names (K V cache sometimes appears as spelled out), small punctuation errors. There were a few overlaps when multiple attendees chimed in during the cost discussion.
